taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): flowering stems erect, often branched, 40-80 cm tall; Gleason and Cronquist (1991) give 4-8 dm; the page itself could not be opened from here, so the wording is as a web-search excerpt quoted it (2026-10-17).

traits.life_span.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): herbaceous perennials.

traits.woodiness.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): herbaceous perennials.

traits.perennation.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): a mat-forming perennial; read as spreading by creeping stems at the ground, drawn as a rhizome's clump (inferred).

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): its rosettes keep their leaves through the year in the gardens it is grown in (read from the article's cultivation notes; inferred for the wild plant).

traits.rosette.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): basal leaves with blades oblong-elliptic, about 10 cm long and 2.5 cm wide, below the flowering stems.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): the leaves are arranged oppositely on the stems.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): leaves 5 to 10 cm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): basal leaves about 10 cm long and 2.5 cm wide; the range round that width is ours.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): basal blades oblong-elliptic, the apex attenuate, gradually narrowed to a rounded point.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): leaf margins crenulate but covered with dense hairs.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): leaves densely covered on both sides with grey-silver, silky-lanate hairs; Gleason and Cronquist (1991): densely white-tomentose throughout with long matted hairs; the page itself could not be opened from here, so the wording is as a web-search excerpt quoted it (2026-10-17).

traits.leaf_hairs_beneath.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): densely covered on both sides with silky-lanate hairs, the undersides more silver-white than the tops.

traits.leaf_hair_length_m.note: About 3 mm, single long wavy hairs measured by eye on iNaturalist photographs with a ring for scale (observations 171598444, 238297511): 2-5 mm. No published measurement could be reached.

traits.stem_hairs.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): usually densely covered with grey or silver-white, silky-lanate hairs; Gleason and Cronquist (1991): white-tomentose throughout; the page itself could not be opened from here, so the wording is as a web-search excerpt quoted it (2026-10-17).

traits.hair_colour.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): grey or silver-white hairs. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): flowering spikes 10-22 cm long of crowded whorls (verticillasters) of many flowers on no pedicels.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): flowering spikes 10-22 cm long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): corollas 1.2 cm long.

traits.flower_colour.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): pink to purple flowers, the corollas veined darker purple inside. The colour is our reading of the words and of iNaturalist photographs (observation 169267090).

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Wikipedia, Stachys byzantina (article text read 2026-10-17): two-lipped corollas, as in the genus.

traits.fruit_type.note: Four nutlets in the persistent calyx, as Lamiaceae fruit (the family file reads its fruit as a schizocarp of four mericarps); not checked for this species.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: About 2 mm, the size of a Stachys nutlet, hidden in the woolly calyx; our estimate, as no measurement for this species could be reached.

traits.flowering_months.note: Summer flowering, as Wikipedia says (in summer it sends up flowering stems); June-August are our reading for the northern temperate gardens and roadsides it grows in.

generator.params.note: Hand-set after Wikipedia's description: a low mat of rosettes of thick oblong leaves 10 cm long (basal_leaves 12 at each stem's foot, spread nearly flat, basal_angle 70) from which erect, few-leaved flowering stems 40-80 cm tall rise in summer, their leaves in opposite pairs, a little smaller up the stem (leaf_top 0.75), each stem ending in one spike of crowded whorls of small flowers on no stalks (flowers 1: the spike is the flowering organ, its size and flowers from inflorescence_length_m and flower_size_m). Stems from the second year; a first-year plant is its rosettes. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.55 m in its second summer in the open, flowering: Wikipedia's flowering stems 40-80 cm, Gleason and Cronquist's 4-8 dm. Not measured.

appearance.note: By eye, after Wikipedia and Gleason and Cronquist: a grey-green face (the wool's white is drawn by its hairs, `leaf_hairs`), oblong-elliptic blades narrowed to a rounded tip on a short stalk, and magenta-pink flowers half hidden in the wool, as iNaturalist photographs show them (observations 238297511, 169267090, 63744082).
